recipes.name: Easy Leftover Potato Pancakes
ingredients_raw: 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, or as needed

steps.text: Mix potatoes, cheese, beaten egg, and salt in a medium bowl until well combined. If the mixture is very wet, mix in flour as needed to bind mixture together.
Melt butter on a large griddle over medium heat.
Drop potato mixture onto the hot griddle, 1/4 cup at a time.
Flatten each pancake with the back of a spatula to 1/2-inch thickness.
Fry until golden brown, about 5 minutes per side. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Leftover Potato Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: Wondering what to do with leftover mashed potatoes? Make these easy, cheesy potato pancakes; serve with fried eggs for a delicious breakfast or brunch.

review.reviewBody: My Mom has been making these since I can remember, but without the cheddar cheese. The cheese makes them much better. I serve them as a side - as you would hash browns - with bacon & eggs. Frying them in the bacon pan doesn't hurt either. The only reason I didn't give this recipe 5 stars is that it's not quite as good as potato latkes. But, it is good and is a great use of leftover mashed potatoes. If you're making these for the first time, I recommend green onions or chives. Also, be sure to make the pancakes more like the size of sausage patties. If you make them too big, they'll fall apart when you turn them. Thanks for sharing this Deanne.

These potatoe pancakes were awesome. I did add 1/3 cup flour to pancakes together. I also added a splash of milk to get the right consistency and bacon bits. Served with sour cream. So delicious...Will definately make them again...Thanks...

Delicious!! I read several of the reviews before making my batch. I needed to use up some leftover mashed potatoes. They were lightly seasoned, so I added in plenty of cheese, green onions, bacon bits, a touch of minced garlic, and a tsp of salt. I also added in 3T of Gluten-free Bisquick, as recommended by many reviewers. I used a large skillet, 2T butter to sautee the pancakes. I formed the pancakes by hand and smooshed them down a bit. It made about 8. I cooked on medium heat for about 5-8 minutes on each side. They were perfect! Crispy outside, warm and creamy inside.

If you find that your potato mixture is too runny, just add instant potato flakes instead of flour. Also you'll want to chill these prior to cooking to help alleviate the 'falling apart' problem. What I did was scoop them out with an ice cream scooper, rolled them in panko, placed them on a plate and stuck them in the fridge. When you're ready to cook them, just squish them down a bit when they go in the pan so you're not trying to fry a ball! :) Experiment a bit with spices like minced onion, garlic powder, or even ranch mix! For the basic recipe I'm giving this five stars...they're great if you're careful with prep and execution. Thank you!

YUMMY, YUMMY, YUMMY!!!! This is the only Potato Pancake recipe you need. After reviewing other people's feedback here are some additions that I made. I added chopped up leftover bacon (could do the same with sausage), three tablespoons of flour, a pinch of garlic salt, a pinch of pepper, and onion to taste (recommend you fry up the onion first). Recommend you make them a little bigger then a sausage patty. I made six nice size pancakes with the current measurements. Recommend doubling if you are cooking for more then just three people. Cook on medium heat. Be patient, if you cook them too high you will burn them and the middle will not firm up. This one is husband approved!

I added 1 more egg, 1/4 cup o flour and 1/4 of fresh chives. I fried them in bacon fat with oil and butter - just a small amount in a cast iron skillet on medium. They have been awesome both times I've made them.
It’s a great base recipe for leftover mashed potatoes . I added an extra egg and 1/2 cup chopped onions (or 2 tablespoons dried chopped onion).

One of my favorite things about this site is reading all the reviews! I added a bit of flour and more seasoning as others suggested, along with some chopped onion (would have preferred chives or scallions but none on hand!) The guide to measurements and cooking method and time was key for me, that's where I need help and guidance. These got two thumbs up from me and hub. We're looking forward to having mashed potatoes again just so I can make the pancakes again!

This is almost exactly how I use all my leftover mashed potatoes. A couple of changes I did to my recipe is adding a lot more onion (my family just prefers them that way) I also add a bit of baking powder to make them rise a bit. I also shred up a potato and squeeze the liquid out to help add more texture to them sometimes. This is a great recipe. You can also use leftover spaghetti squash instead of the potatoes. They're a bit sweeter but still very good.

I used 2 1/2 cups of potatoes and 1 cup of Bisquick, added onions, a 1/2 tps of cayenne and kosher salt. Cooked on low. Be sure to could at least 10 minutes or more to make turning easier! They were delicious!

Delicious! I took the advice of another reviewer and added a 1/3 cup of flour, other than that I followed the directions exactly. I found that 5 minutes on each side was a little too long, so on my second batch I only cooked them for 4 minutes on each side and they were golden and perfect. Will definitely make again! What a great way to use left over mashed potatoes!

I cut this in half and used almost 1/4 cup sharp cheddar cheese and the full egg. It did take close to 1/4 c. of flour to get these to the texture I wanted. I used those refrigerated pre made mashed potatoes from the deli case, the Bob Evan's ones and they worked out great. This was a nice potatoey flavor and the cheddar cheese really made these creamy and rich. These would be nice with some chives added and a dollop of sour cream on top. I used lingonberry jam which was fine, but ketchup might have worked just as well since it goes with potatoes.
This is the perfect way to use leftover mashed potatoes. Easy easy easy.
